open.title: regression/race makes dynamic routes 404 on big apps
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/juliangruber/next-dev-partial-scan-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install` (a postinstall script generates 5000 small filler pages/API routes so the initial scan has realistic size)
2. `npm run add-probe` — adds two `console.error` lines to `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-utils/setup-dev-bundler.js` so the watcher's aggregation behavior is observable (no behavior change)
3. `npx next dev`
4. Watch the `[AGG-PROBE]` lines; optionally request `GET /api/123` (dynamic) and `GET /api/hello` (static) as soon as the server accepts connections. Background I/O+CPU load widens the window if the first aggregation comes back complete on your machine.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** the dev server can report ready (and resolve `prepare()` for custom servers) while the initial pages-directory scan is still in flight. Observed on the fresh clone with no synthetic load:

```
[AGG-PROBE] aggregated fired at 1784883621550
[AGG-PROBE] routedPages count: 1 dynamic routes: 0 at 1784883621577    <-- this one gates readiness
[AGG-PROBE] aggregated fired at 1784883621955
[AGG-PROBE] routedPages count: 5003 dynamic routes: 1 at 1784883622185
```

The first `aggregated` callback saw 1 of 5003 pages and 0 dynamic routes, so `fsChecker.dynamicRoutes` is built from a nearly empty page list. Until a later aggregation rebuilds it, **every dynamic pages-router route returns the 404 page with `text/html`, while static routes keep working** (they resolve via on-demand filesystem checks instead of the dynamic-route table). In this minimal repro the window is a few hundred ms; on a loaded machine running a large app (~1000 pages, custom Express server) we observed the broken state 17+ seconds after listen, and it persists until the next aggregation.

**Cause:** #83628 (Next 16) lowered the dev watcher's watchpack `aggregateTimeout` from the 200ms default to 5ms. Watchpack's initial scan emits one change event per pre-existing file and fires `aggregated` `aggregateTimeout` ms after the *last* event. Any >5ms delay mid-scan fires the first aggregation with a partial `wp.getTimeInfoEntries()`. A control run with `aggregateTimeout: 200` (the pre-16 value) produces a single complete first aggregation (5003/5003, dynamic route present) even under heavy load.

**Expected:** readiness should gate on initial-scan completion, not on an aggregation-timer tick that can fire mid-scan. The first aggregation used for the route tables should always contain the complete page list (as it usually did with the 200ms default in Next ≤15).

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.5.0: Tue Jun  9 22:28:34 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.121.10~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050
  Available memory (MB): 49152
  Available CPU cores: 18
Binaries:
  Node: 24.14.1
  npm: 11.11.0
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 10.34.5
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.0-canary.95
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.1.1
  react-dom: 19.1.1
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Dynamic Routes, Pages Router

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local)

### Additional context

- Introduced by #83628 ("Development: Make 'ready in' 195ms faster", first in 16.0.0); reproduced on 16.2.6 and 16.3.0-canary.95. Not bundler-specific: the same `startWatcher` watchpack callback builds `fsChecker.dynamicRoutes` for both Turbopack and webpack dev.
- Reproduces with plain `next dev`; also affects custom servers, where the partial first aggregation resolves `nextApp.prepare()`.
- Downstream workaround we're shipping (restores the pre-16 value via a package patch): https://github.com/SocketDev/depscan/pull/23093 (private repo, linked for cross-reference).

open.title: next start (HTTP/1.1): router prefetch burst exhausts the browser connection pool and stalls/aborts Server Action round-trips — deterministic repro included
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/SignaHub285/next-app-router-action-abort-repro

### To Reproduce

Run `npm i && npm run repro` in the linked repository (it builds the app, starts `next start` behind a small RSC-delay proxy, and prints a measured PASS/FAIL).


Self-hosted `next start` serves the browser over **plain HTTP/1.1**, where Chrome allows at most **6 connections per origin**. The repro turns the resulting race into a deterministic, measured demonstration:

1. `npm i && npm run repro` — builds the app, starts `next start`, and puts a ~40-line HTTP/1.1 latency proxy (`scripts/slow-rsc-proxy.mjs`) in front of it. The proxy holds each App Router `_rsc` **prefetch** response open ~4s and streams everything else through, emulating a busy 2-core CI runner. It then drives a real Chromium (Playwright) through the **same** scenario twice:
   - **control** — prefetch pressure off (stands in for HTTP/2, which has no per-origin connection cap);
   - **treatment** — the `_rsc` prefetch burst kept topped up, so all 6 HTTP/1.1 sockets stay occupied.
2. Each run navigates client-side home → `/status` (which fires the prefetch burst for the ~60 sidebar `<Link>`s), then clicks **Mark ready** — a Server Action that flips a server-side value `draft → ready` and calls `revalidatePath("/status")`.
3. The script polls both the rendered UI and the server truth (`GET /api/state`, fetched straight from upstream so it bypasses the browser pool), and prints a PASS/FAIL banner.

The real-world trigger is the ordinary one: a dashboard/sidebar layout, a client-side navigation, and a Server Action submitted a beat later — on a slow enough machine the prefetches are still in flight (CI runners qualify). We chased this for days as "flaky e2e" before isolating the transport as the cause.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** while the six HTTP/1.1 connections are held by the prefetch burst, the Server Action's round trip is stalled — the click does nothing and the UI stays frozen on the pre-action server-component value for the entire time the pool is saturated. Several in-flight `_rsc` requests are aborted (`net::ERR_ABORTED`) along the way. The proxy releases the pool after ~4s so the demo self-heals then; on a real runner where the prefetch responses stay slow the pool never drains and it hangs until a hard reload. Depending on exactly when the action's socket frees, this presents either as the action "hanging" / "forever pending" (#55814, #53966) or as "the mutation committed but the client kept the stale server-component props" — I've observed both, including a stale + aborted-POST outcome firing spontaneously.

Actual output of `npm run repro` (same code, same click, both runs):

```
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 Server Action under HTTP/1.1 prefetch-pool exhaustion
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 CONTROL   (pool OK ≈ HTTP/2)   UI updated after click : 278ms
                               timeline (250ms/step)  : dRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR
 TREATMENT (HTTP/1.1 pool full) UI updated after click : 3876ms
                               timeline (250ms/step)  : dddddddddddddddRRRRRRRRR
                               at 2500ms → UI="draft", server="draft"
                               aborted RSC requests   : 6 (e.g. GET /item/39?_rsc=...)
  legend: d = UI shows "draft" (pre-action)   R = UI shows "ready"   . = transient
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 PASS ✅  BUG REPRODUCED
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

**Expected:** the App Router should not let its own prefetch traffic starve a Server Action on HTTP/1.1. Concretely, one or more of: cap/queue router prefetch concurrency below the HTTP/1.1 connection limit (or deprioritize prefetches when an action is pending); detect an aborted action/revalidation and retry or surface an error instead of leaving the router silently stalled; and at minimum document that `next start` behind HTTP/1.1 is subject to this and recommend an h2 front for self-hosting and e2e.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.5.0
  Available CPU cores: 18
Binaries:
  Node: 22.23.0
  npm: 10.9.8
  pnpm: 11.6.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.11 // Latest available version is detected (16.2.11).
  react: 19.2.8
  react-dom: 19.2.8
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

Also reproduced on Linux 2-core CI runners. `cacheComponents` is enabled to mirror the original app, but the failure is a transport-level property of the HTTP/1.1 pool and does not depend on it.

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Server Actions, Linking and Navigating, Output

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local)

### Additional context

- **Not reproducible over HTTP/2.** The same build deployed on Vercel, or self-hosted behind any HTTP/2 reverse proxy (Caddy/nginx/Cloudflare), updates immediately — h2 multiplexes and there is no 6-connection cap. The `control` run in the repro demonstrates this by disabling the pool pressure; it always repaints in well under a second. Also not reproducible in `next dev`.
- This re-files #96101, which was auto-closed for lacking a reproduction link — this issue supplies one. It is very likely the same transport-level root cause behind the long-open "Server Actions hang indefinitely" / "forever pending" reports (#55814, #53966), which never identified a mechanism: the symptom matches and the fix direction is the same.
- The repo is built from the official reproduction-template shape; the only additions are the sidebar of links (the prefetch burst), the Server Action + `revalidatePath`, the `GET /api/state` ground-truth probe, the latency proxy, and a small client component that keeps the prefetch burst topped up so the condition is steady enough to observe on a fast dev machine (it issues only GETs the app already serves and mutates nothing; the control run disables it).



_Prior filings #96101 and #96108 were bot-closed on link-format technicalities; this one follows the form field format exactly._

open.title: Turbopack: poisoned persistent cache panics all workers on restore ("Every task must have a task type") — deadlocked compiles, ~900% CPU idle spin, OOM crash loop
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/shashwat46/turbopack-persistent-cache-panic-repro

### To Reproduce

The failure state is a **poisoned Turbopack persistent cache** (`.next/dev/cache/turbopack`, 2.1 GB of RocksDB-style `.sst` files). Restoring it and running `next dev` reproduces the failure **deterministically, every time**:

1. `next dev` boots normally (`✓ Ready in 231ms`)
2. within seconds — before any HTTP request — ~10 tokio workers panic:

```
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at turbopack/crates/turbo-tasks-backend/src/backend/operation/mod.rs:966:13:
Every task must have a task type TaskGuard { task_id: TaskId { id: 2147485064 }, storage: TaskStorage {
  ... persistent_task_type: None,
  flags: TaskFlags { ... meta_restored: true, data_restored: true, ... },
  lazy: [InProgress(Scheduled { done_event: Event, reason: ActivateInitial })] } }
```

3. any request needing fresh compilation hangs forever (`GET /` > 60 s, no response)
4. under interactive use the process settles into **600–975% CPU while fully idle** (verified: no requests for 30+ min, zero fs events in the watched tree). A macOS `sample` shows all tokio workers on-CPU inside `next-swc` with spin-lock yields (`cthread_yield`/`swtch_pri`) at the leaves, and worker thread IDs climbing continuously (panic → respawn cycle)
5. RSS oscillates 1 → 4.8 GB until the server dies (OOM); the `next dev` wrapper/user restarts it and the cycle repeats. This burned ~2.5 hours across 3 boots before diagnosis.

The linked repo contains a minimal app matching the failing versions, the sanitized boot log, the `sample` stack analysis, and the invalidation-marker evidence. The poisoned cache itself embeds compiled proprietary application code, so it is retained privately — **available to maintainers on request**, including running instrumented builds against it.

Suspected corruption origin: torn write during cache persist on hard process death (SIGKILL/OOM — note this bug's own OOM loop makes that recurrent). `.sst` timestamps place the poisoning in the prior evening's dev session.

**Self-healing also failed in the wild:** the affected instance wrote `.next/dev/cache/turbopack/__turbo_tasks_invalidated_db` (`"reason_code": "turbo_tasks_backend::database::db_invalidation::invalidation_reasons::PANIC"`) mid-run — and then kept grinding the poisoned DB at ~900% CPU for 30+ more minutes instead of discarding it; a later boot still restored poisoned tasks with that marker present on disk. To be fair: in controlled replays (marker planted into healthy and poisoned caches, with/without `NEXT_TURBOPACK_TRACING`), startup honored the marker correctly — the wild non-honoring seems to need an extra condition we could not isolate (in-place DB state vs a fresh copy, or timing around the mid-run marker write).

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current: a restored task with `persistent_task_type: None` panics the worker pool → deadlocked compiles + idle CPU spin + OOM crash loop, recurring on every restart because the poisoned DB stays on disk.

Expected:
1. a restored task without a task type invalidates the cache and falls back to a cold build — never a panic loop
2. an instance that writes the PANIC invalidation marker stops trusting the poisoned DB immediately (cold restart of turbo-tasks), rather than continuing to spin against it

Workaround (verified): `rm -rf .next/dev/cache/turbopack` → panics 10 → 0, `GET /` from infinite hang → 200 in 4.7 s, idle CPU 975% → 0.2%.

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin  Arch: arm64 (M-series, 10 cores, 24 GB)
  Version: Darwin 25.5.0
Binaries:
  Node: 26.3.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.6 (Turbopack, default)
  react: 19.2.6
  react-dom: 19.2.6
  typescript: 5.9.3
```

Canary note: could not verify on canary — the poisoned artifact is version-keyed to 16.2.6, and a synthetic corruption could not be fabricated in the minimal app so far. Release notes for 16.2.7–16.2.11 mention no related fix.

### Which area(s) are affected?

Turbopack, Persistent caching

### Additional context

Almost certainly the same underlying bug as #93896 (identical symptoms: 16.2.6, M-series, 600%+ CPU; auto-closed without diagnosis). Earlier filings of this diagnosis (#96091, #96092) were auto-closed by the triage bot over the reproduction-link section format — this issue supersedes both.

open.title: OpenTelemetry HttpInstrumentation set up via instrumentation.ts never instruments incoming requests — http is loaded before register() and no later require passes the hook
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/r34son/next-otel-http-instrumentation-repro

### To Reproduce

1. npm install && npm run build && npm run start (standalone output, node .next/standalone/server.js)
2. curl -sI http://localhost:3000/ | grep -i x-otel-trace-id

The repro uses the OpenTelemetry setup from the [Next.js OpenTelemetry guide (manual configuration)](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/open-telemetry#manual-opentelemetry-configuration) — NodeSDK initialized from instrumentation.ts — plus @opentelemetry/instrumentation-http@0.219.0 with a responseHook that sets an x-otel-trace-id response header, used as an externally observable marker of whether the instrumentation handles incoming requests.

Control experiment in the same repo: npm run start:preload loads the exact same SDK setup via NODE_OPTIONS="--require ./otel-preload.cjs" instead of instrumentation.ts.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:**

| Setup | `x-otel-trace-id` header | HTTP server spans |
|---|---|---|
| via `instrumentation.ts`, next@16.2.10 (Turbopack build) | 0/3 requests | none — every exported span has `instrumentationScope: next.js` |
| via `instrumentation.ts`, next@15.5.20 (webpack build, same files) | 0/3 requests | none |
| same code via `NODE_OPTIONS="--require"`, either version | 3/3 requests | present |

The failure is completely silent: the SDK starts fine (`[repro] OTel NodeSDK started` is printed), Next's built-in `next.js`-scoped spans flow, and `trace.getSpanContext(context.active())` returns valid contexts during SSR — which masks the fact that `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-http` never attached. There is no warning (the `"Module http has been loaded before…"` diag warning is only visible if a diag logger is configured).

**Expected:** instrumentations registered in `instrumentation.ts` `register()` — the place the OpenTelemetry guide recommends — instrument incoming HTTP requests, or at least the limitation is documented in the OpenTelemetry guide.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin 25.5.0
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 22.18.0
  npm: 10.9.3
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.10 // Latest available version is detected (16.2.10).
  react: 19.2.3
  react-dom: 19.2.3
Next.js Config:
  output: standalone


Also reproduces with next@15.5.20 (webpack) on the same environment.
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Instrumentation

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local)

### Additional context

## Root cause

`HttpInstrumentation` patches `http`/`https` through `require-in-the-middle`, which wraps `Module.prototype.require` and applies the patch on the **next** `require('http')` call passing through it (a cache hit is fine — it still goes through the wrapped require).

1. In standalone mode the generated `server.js` requires `next/dist/server/lib/start-server`, which imports `http`/`https` at module top — long before `register()` runs: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/v15.5.12/packages/next/src/server/lib/start-server.ts#L18-L19
2. `register()` is invoked much later, from `prepare()` of an already-listening server: `startServer()` → `server.listen` → `getRequestHandlers` → `NextServer.prepare` → `loadInstrumentationModule` → `prepareImpl` → `runInstrumentationHookIfAvailable` (see `packages/next/src/server/base-server.ts` / `next-server.ts`).
3. Nothing guarantees a `require('http')` **after** `register()`: page preloading (`unstable_preloadEntries`, which deliberately awaits `prepare()` first — “Ensure prepare process will be finished before preloading entries”) does run after `register()`, but the bundler's externals factories for `http` inside route chunks evaluate lazily and, for most pages, never; the externals factory of the `instrumentation` chunk itself evaluates while that chunk is being imported, i.e. *before* the hook is armed inside `register()`. So whether the instrumentation ever attaches depends on the accidental import graph of the app — a hello-world never wins this race, and a larger app wins or loses it per bundle graph.

The mechanism is confirmed by an OpenTelemetry maintainer in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js-contrib#3209: “if Next internally imports or requires the `http` module before we've had a chance to patch it, it won't be patched” — with `--require` suggested as the only reliable option (which defeats the purpose of `instrumentation.ts`, and breaks `.env` loading).

A 10-line proof without Next behaves identically: load `http`, create a server, then start the SDK — no patch ever; a single fresh `require('http')` afterwards — patched, header present on the very next request.

## Related issues

- #64879 — same class of problem, framed as “native modules imported from `instrumentation.ts` are cached before `register()`”. This repro shows it is broader: it fails even when `instrumentation.ts` imports nothing http-related, because Next's own `start-server` import is what caches `http`.
- #80262 — the same defect observed as “`http_server_request_duration` metrics are never collected” (those metrics are produced by `instrumentation-http`).
- #51233 — conflicts that appear in the cases when `HttpInstrumentation` *does* manage to attach.

## Workarounds

- `NODE_OPTIONS="--require ./otel-preload.cjs"` — works (see control experiment), but bypasses `instrumentation.ts` entirely and has known downsides (`.env` not loaded yet, extra ops surface).
- `require-in-the-middle` >= 7.4 also hooks [`process.getBuiltinModule`](https://github.com/elastic/require-in-the-middle/blob/v7.4.0/index.js#L145-L147), so one call right after `sdk.start()` inside `register()` applies the pending patch to the already-loaded core modules (public Node >= 20.16 API, untouched by bundlers):

  ```js
  sdk.start();
  process.getBuiltinModule('http');
  process.getBuiltinModule('https');
  ```

- Things that do **not** work: `createRequire()` (its require bypasses `Module.prototype.require`, the hook never sees it); a bare `require('http')` in bundled code (compiled into the bundler's own runtime shim); moving the SDK setup to the top level of `instrumentation.ts` (placement makes no difference — setups that appear to work after this change work because their import graph happens to issue hooked loads after arming, e.g. `@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node`, and they work inside `register()` too).

It would be great if Next either performed a module-system pass for core modules after `register()` (a single `process.getBuiltinModule('http')`-style touch would do), or documented this pitfall and the escape hatch in the OpenTelemetry guide.

open.title: cacheComponents: runtime ISR revalidation fails with a message-less StaticGenBailoutError — the real reason only reaches console.error, so error trackers get an empty, unactionable event
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/qnten/sentry-cache-components-repro

### To Reproduce

The linked repro (from getsentry/sentry-javascript#21333) demonstrates the underlying trigger — a sync-IO violation recorded during a prerender. This report is about **how that failure surfaces at runtime**: the thrown error carries no message, while the actual reason only goes to `console.error`.

1. `cacheComponents: true`, a fully static route (no Suspense boundary) whose section fetcher catches backend errors and, in the catch, calls something that does sync IO — e.g. `Sentry.captureException` (→ `crypto.randomUUID()`) with `@sentry/nextjs` < 10.57.0, or any uncached `Date.now()` / `Math.random()`. Note the patched globals record the violation **without throwing** ("The extensions here never error" — `node-environment-extensions/web-crypto.js`), so user code cannot guard against it with try/catch.
2. Deploy to Vercel. Let the backend read fail during a **background ISR revalidation** (`handleRevalidate`), so the catch path runs inside the runtime prerender.
3. The revalidation aborts. `onRequestError` (and any APM hooked into it) receives the thrown error.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** `throwIfDisallowedDynamic` (`packages/next/src/server/app-render/dynamic-rendering.ts`) throws `new StaticGenBailoutError()` — no message, no cause — at every throw site, immediately after `logDisallowedDynamicError(workStore, error)` printed the real explanation ("Route "/" used `crypto.randomUUID()` before accessing … next-prerender-crypto", plus the `--debug-prerender` hint) to `console.error` only.

What an error tracker receives in production is an event with type `Error`, an **empty message**, and a minified runtime stack (`function H(e,t,r,n){if(n.syncDynamic…`). Real example from our production (Sentry, `mechanism: auto.function.nextjs.on_request_error`, `transaction: GET /page`):

```
Error:
  File ".../next-server/app-page-turbo.runtime.prod.js", line 5, in H
  ...
  File ".../app-page-turbo.runtime.prod.js", line 17, in nh.handleRevalidate
```

Diagnosing this requires correlating short-retention Vercel function logs with the APM event, or reading the minified runtime. It cost us a full source-dive to map `H` → `throwIfDisallowedDynamic`.

**Expected:** the thrown `StaticGenBailoutError` carries the reason it already has in hand — e.g. constructed with `serverDynamic.syncDynamicErrorWithStack.message` / the first `dynamicValidation.dynamicErrors[i].message`, or with the original error as `cause`. The information is computed at every throw site; this looks like a one-line change per site and makes runtime revalidation failures self-explanatory in error trackers.

### Provide environment information

```
Next.js: 16.2.9 (turbopack)
Node: v24.x
Deployment: Vercel (minimal mode), background ISR revalidation
Config: cacheComponents: true
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Partial Prerendering (PPR), Caching (ISR)

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

- The most common way to land in this state was `Sentry.captureException` inside a catch during a revalidation — Sentry has since made their SDK safe (getsentry/sentry-javascript#21333, #21510) — but any disallowed-dynamic violation during a runtime revalidation produces the same message-less error, so the surfacing problem is framework-level, not SDK-specific.
- Because the patched globals are deliberately transparent (never throw), the *only* record of the reason is stdout. On Vercel that means the diagnosis window is the function-log retention window.

open.title: Turbopack ignores custom Emotion cache during SSR when using @mui/material-nextjs (Pages Router)
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/amirdevir/nextjs-mui-rtl-turbopack-reproduction

### To Reproduce

1. Create a Next.js 16 project using Pages Router.
2. Install @mui/material, @mui/material-nextjs and Emotion.
3. Configure RTL using createEmotionCache(), AppCacheProvider and documentGetInitialProps().
4. Run the project with `next dev`.
5. Open any SSR page.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

# Bug Report

## Description

After upgrading to **Next.js 16**, **React 19**, and **MUI 9**, I encountered an SSR issue that only occurs when running the application with **Turbopack**.

The project uses the **Pages Router** together with **@mui/material-nextjs** and follows the official MUI SSR integration guide.

With Turbopack, the custom Emotion cache is not used during server-side rendering, causing RTL styles to be missing on the initial page load.

The exact same project works correctly when switching to Webpack without making any code changes.

---

## Environment

* Next.js: 16.2.x
* React: 19.2.x
* React DOM: 19.2.x
* Pages Router
* Turbopack
* Node.js: v24.15.0

Related packages:

* @mui/material: 9.2.0
* @mui/material-nextjs: 9.1.1
* @emotion/cache: 11.14.0
* @emotion/react: 11.14.0
* @emotion/styled: 11.14.1
* @mui/stylis-plugin-rtl: 9.1.1

---

## Reproduction

The application follows the official MUI Pages Router integration.

### Emotion cache

```ts
import { createEmotionCache } from "@mui/material-nextjs/v16-pagesRouter";
import rtlPlugin from "@mui/stylis-plugin-rtl";

export function createRtlCache() {
  return createEmotionCache({
    key: "muirtl",
    enableCssLayer: true,
    stylisPlugins: [rtlPlugin],
  });
}
```

### _document.tsx

```ts
import {
  documentGetInitialProps,
} from "@mui/material-nextjs/v16-pagesRouter";

MyDocument.getInitialProps = async (ctx) => {
  return await documentGetInitialProps(ctx, {
    emotionCache: createRtlCache(),
  });
};
```

### _app.tsx

```tsx
const clientEmotionCache = createRtlCache();

<AppCacheProvider emotionCache={clientEmotionCache}>
  <Component {...pageProps} />
</AppCacheProvider>
```

`<Html dir="rtl">` is also configured correctly.

---

## Expected behavior

During SSR, the custom Emotion cache should be used.

The generated styles should look similar to:

```html
<style data-emotion="muirtl ...">
```

RTL styles should be applied correctly on the initial server render.

---

## Actual behavior

When running with Turbopack:

* SSR generates styles using the default Emotion cache (`css`) instead of the provided cache (`muirtl`).
* The page is rendered without RTL styles.
* After navigating using `next/link`, RTL styles become correct because the client cache is used.

The initial HTML contains:

```html
<style data-emotion="css ...">
```

instead of

```html
<style data-emotion="muirtl ...">
```

---

## Additional observations

While inspecting the rendered page, two different Emotion cache prefixes are generated.

Components rendered during SSR receive classes such as:

```text
css-10360ue
```

while components rendered after client-side navigation receive:

```text
muirtl-10360ue
```

As a result, the same component receives different class names depending on whether it was rendered on the server or the client.

---

## Investigation

The following have already been verified:

* Only one `AppCacheProvider` exists.
* Only one custom Emotion cache is created.
* Only one `emotion-insertion-point` meta tag exists.
* No additional `CacheProvider` is used.
* No duplicate `ThemeProvider` exists.
* The implementation follows the official MUI documentation.
* The issue occurs only during SSR.

---

## Critical finding

Changing only the development server from:

```bash
next dev
```

to

```bash
next dev --webpack
```

completely resolves the issue.

Without changing any application code:

* SSR uses the custom Emotion cache correctly.
* Generated styles use the `muirtl` cache key.
* RTL styles are applied correctly.
* Only a single Emotion cache is present.

This strongly suggests the issue is specific to Turbopack rather than the MUI integration itself.

---

## Expected outcome

open.title: Turbopack 16.3: nft.json drops store target files for an ESM serverExternalPackage reached via a 'use client' component in a shared SSR-layer chunk → dangling alias → ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on Vercel
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/cipriancaba/next-turbopack-nft-ssr-chunk-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `bun install` (bun **isolated** linker, set via the repo's `bunfig.toml` — produces the `node_modules/.bun` store)
2. `bun run build` (Turbopack `next build` of `apps/web`)
3. `node check-nft.mjs` — per-endpoint `.nft.json` verifier: for every content-hashed external alias referenced by an endpoint's trace, it resolves the imported specifiers through the package's `exports` map and checks the store target files are in that same trace.

The scaffold reproduces the mechanism **up to the ssr-only chunk placement** (see "partial" note below): `@ai-sdk/google` + `ai/internal`, imported via a `'use client'` component, land in `server/chunks/ssr/…` chunks only. The final failing step — a **shared cross-route** ssr chunk — only emerges at app-scale module counts, which is why clean public repros of this bug are scarce; the `analysis/` directory ships the chunk-level evidence extracted from a real app-scale production build where the traces do go dangling, plus the analyzer to reproduce that extraction on any affected build.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** on `next@16.3.0-preview.6` (and canary.86), for endpoints whose `.nft.json` includes a shared SSR-layer chunk referencing an externalized package the endpoint does not itself import, the trace lists the package's content-hashed alias symlink but **not** its store target files. Vercel packs the lambda strictly from the trace → dangling symlink → `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` → HTTP 500 on routes/server actions that never import the package.

**Expected:** as on `16.2.9` — whenever a chunk in an endpoint's trace references an external alias, the alias symlink and its store target files are traced together.

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.4.0
  Available memory (MB): 49152
  Available CPU cores: 18
Binaries:
  Node: 24.14.1
  npm: 11.18.0
  pnpm: 10.33.0
  bun: 1.3.11 (isolated linker)
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.0-preview.6 (also reproduced on 16.3.0-canary.86; 16.2.9 unaffected)
  react: 19.2.6
  react-dom: 19.2.6
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

Turbopack, Output (export/standalone)

### Which stage(s) are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

next build (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

A previous filing of this report (#95815) was auto-closed and locked by the bot before the public reproduction repository was attached; this issue supersedes it. Related umbrella issue: #87737 — that thread describes a "hash mismatch after reinstall" variant; the mechanism below is a distinct trigger sharing the alias/store machinery, and refines my earlier comment there (https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/87737#issuecomment-4897366831).

---

## Summary

Since Next 16.1, Turbopack externalizes server packages behind content-hashed aliases
(`.next/node_modules/<pkg>-<hash>` → a symlink into the package-manager store). On 16.2.9 each
route's `*.nft.json` lists **both** the alias symlink and the store target files, so the packed
lambda resolves. On **16.3** (preview + canary), for a specific class of endpoints the trace lists
the alias symlink **but not the store target files**, so Vercel packs a dangling symlink and every
import of that package throws `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (HTTP 500).

The affected endpoints are precisely those whose nft includes a **shared SSR-layer chunk**
(`.next/server/chunks/ssr/…`) that references an externalized package the endpoint does **not**
import in its own module graph.

## Environment

- `next@16.3.0-preview.6` (also reproduced on `16.3.0-canary.86`); 16.2.9 is unaffected.
- Turbopack (default). App Router, `cacheComponents: true`, partial-prerendered dynamic routes.
- Package manager: bun with the **isolated** linker (store at `node_modules/.bun/<pkg>@<ver>/…`);
  the mechanism is not bun-specific — any linker that produces store symlinks behind the alias
  should show it.

## Root cause / mechanism

1. **The discriminator is the chunk layer.** An externalized package whose alias appears only in
   `server/chunks/ssr/…` chunks (the layer that server-renders `'use client'` components) has its
   store target dropped; the same package referenced from a non-ssr (react-server) chunk traces
   fine. The reference form is identical in both — the async external loader `a.y("<alias>")` — so
   it is not about ESM vs CJS or the call site.

2. **How a server-only package reaches the ssr layer:** it is imported (transitively) by a
   `'use client'` component (e.g. a UI package's client components that import `ai` / `ai/internal`,
   or a `'use server'` action pulled in by a client component that imports `@ai-sdk/google`).

3. **Shared ssr chunk = the failure.** Turbopack merges such client components into a **shared**
   ssr chunk. Every route whose nft lists that shared chunk emits the package's alias symlink
   (the specifier string is physically in the chunk) — but the endpoint tracer only traces the
   store target files for endpoints whose **own module graph** reaches the package. Endpoints that
   merely pull the shared chunk (e.g. an unrelated auth page that never imports the package) get the
   alias **without** its store files → dangling.

## Concrete evidence (from a production build)

In one app's `next build`, a single shared ssr chunk
`server/chunks/ssr/[root-of-the-server]__<hash>._.js` references the `@ai-sdk/google` alias and is
listed in **13** route `*.nft.json` files — including a sign-in/auth page that never imports
`@ai-sdk/google` anywhere in its own source. Each of those 13 nfts contains the
`@ai-sdk/google-<hash>` alias symlink and **zero** `…/.bun/@ai-sdk+google@…/…` store files.

Healthy counter-examples in the **same build** — `resend`, `postcss`, `prettier` — use the identical
`a.y("<alias>")` external form but are also referenced from **non-ssr** chunks, and their store
target files are traced correctly in every nft.

Per-package signature in that build (unambiguous "alias present, zero store files"):

| package | endpoints with alias but zero store files |
|---|---|
| `@ai-sdk/google` | 13 |
| `ai` (root) | 5, plus the `ai/internal` subpath target dropped on 8 more |
| `@aws-sdk/client-s3` | 3 |
| `pdf-lib` | 1 |

### Sanitized excerpts

Content hashes are redacted to `<hash>`; no application source is included — the only chunk
fragment shown is Turbopack's generic external-loader wrapper.

**(a) The shared SSR chunk references the external via the async external loader** (this exact
`a.y(...)` call is the whole reference; the surrounding code is app bundle and is omitted):

```js
// server/chunks/ssr/[root-of-the-server]__<hash>._.js
a.y("@ai-sdk/google-<hash>")
```

That one shared ssr chunk is listed in **13** route `*.nft.json` files.

**(b) A route that never imports `@ai-sdk/google` — its nft has the alias symlink but zero store
files:**

```
# <route>/page.js.nft.json  (a sign-in route; grep of its file list)
../../../../../node_modules/@ai-sdk/google-<hash>      # 1 alias symlink entry
.bun/@ai-sdk+google@…/…                                # 0 store-target entries
```

**(c) Healthy counter-example, same build — `resend`, identical loader form but from a NON-ssr
chunk, store traced:**

```js
// a non-ssr server chunk
a.y("resend-<hash>")
```

```
# a route nft that uses resend
.bun/resend@…/…                                        # 3 store-target entries (traced OK)
```

So the only difference between the dangling `@ai-sdk/google` and the healthy `resend` is the chunk
**layer** (ssr vs non-ssr) and whether the referencing chunk is **shared across routes that do not
own the import** — not the reference form, which is identical.

## Minimal reproduction — partial

A standalone App Router app on `16.3.0-preview.6` (bun isolated linker; `serverExternalPackages:
['ai','@ai-sdk/google','@aws-sdk/client-s3','pdf-lib']`; a `'use client'` component importing
`@ai-sdk/google` + `ai/internal`, rendered by a PPR `[locale]` route) reproduces steps 1–2: the
package lands in an **ssr-only** chunk (`google` referenced from ssr chunks, zero non-ssr). It does
**not** reproduce step 3 in a small app, because at small module counts Turbopack **duplicates** the
ssr chunk per owning route instead of emitting one cross-route **shared** chunk — so no non-owning
route ever lists the alias. Forcing the cross-route ssr **bin-pack** appears to require an app-scale
client-component graph (a barrel re-export does pull the alias cross-route, but it also makes the
route *own* the import, so its store is correctly traced). The scaffold and the `check-nft.mjs`
verifier are available on request.

**Ask:** the endpoint tracer should trace an externalized package's store target files whenever the
endpoint's nft includes a chunk that refe

open.title: next/font/google: allow axes with discrete weight for variable fonts
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/zeinds/next-font-axes-discrete-weight-repro

### To Reproduce

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/zeinds/next-font-axes-discrete-weight-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction repository.
2. Install dependencies.
3. Run `pnpm build` (or `npm run build`).
4. Observe the build error:

   `Axes can only be defined for variable fonts when the weight property is nonexistent or set to variable.`

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior:

`next/font/google` throws when `axes` is combined with a discrete `weight` on a variable font.

Example:

```ts
import { Newsreader } from 'next/font/google';

export const newsreader = Newsreader({
  subsets: ['latin'],
  weight: ['700'],
  style: ['normal'],
  axes: ['opsz'],
  display: 'swap',
});
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

This combination should be allowed.

Google Fonts itself supports this request shape. For example, this URL works:

`https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Newsreader:opsz,wght@6..72,700&display=swap`

So it should be possible for `next/font/google` to request a discrete weight instance of a variable font while still preserving the requested axis.

### Why this matters

Today there are only two workarounds:

1. Use `weight: 'variable'` with `axes`, which keeps the axis but serves the full variable range.
2. Use a discrete `weight` without `axes`, which reduces payload but drops the optical sizing axis.

There is currently no way through `next/font/google` to get both:

- a discrete weight
- and a retained axis such as `opsz`

open.title: next build workers strip --max-old-space-size (isolatedMemory) and expose no memory control — page-data collection OOMs, bundler-independent
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/alexboii/next-build-worker-oom

### To Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alexboii/next-build-worker-oom && cd next-build-worker-oom
docker run --rm -m 4g --cpus 4 -v "$PWD":/app -w /app node:22 bash -c \
  'npm install --no-audit --no-fund && npx next build'
```

The repo contains 12 generated modules that allocate ~150MB each at import time (a stand-in for a large real-world module graph) and 30 Pages Router pages with `getStaticProps` importing them. Full 5-run matrix in the README.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current** (verified in the container above, output committed to the README):

| # | Command | Result |
|---|---------|--------|
| 1 | `npx next build` (11 workers) | `⨯ Next.js build worker exited with code: null and signal: SIGKILL` at `Collecting page data` |
| 2 | `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1024 npx next build` | **identical SIGKILL** — the heap cap has no effect on workers |
| 3 | `experimental.cpus: 1` | passes |
| 4 | `experimental.cpus: 1` + `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1024` | **passes** — the single worker resident-allocates ~1.8GB yet "respects" a 1GB cap, which is only possible because the flag never reaches the worker |
| 5 | `npx next build --webpack` (11 workers) | same SIGKILL — bundler-independent |

Cause: `createStaticWorker` passes `isolatedMemory: true` (`packages/next/src/build/index.ts`, comment: "remove --max-old-space-size flag as it can cause memory issues"), and the Worker wrapper deletes the flag (`packages/next/src/lib/worker.ts`: `delete nodeOptions['max-old-space-size']`). jest-worker's `workerIdleMemoryLimit` is not plumbed through either — so **no configuration bounds build-worker memory at all**.

Run 3's "just lower `cpus`" is not viable at real scale: `experimental.cpus` also sizes static-generation workers, whose memory scales the opposite way (fewer workers ⇒ more pages each ⇒ more memory each). On our production monorepo (~83 static pages, several hundred routes), static generation needs ≥14 workers while page-data collection OOMs at 14 on a 30-vCPU/60GB machine (Vercel's largest) — the window is empty, and we were forced fleet-wide back to webpack + `cpus: 2`, which fits in 16GB. One knob, two opposing constraints, zero memory control.

**Expected** — any one of:
1. An opt-in per-worker heap cap (don't strip `--max-old-space-size` when the user explicitly opts in, e.g. `experimental.staticWorkerMaxOldSpaceSize`), or
2. Memory-bounded worker recycling (expose `workerIdleMemoryLimit`), or
3. Separate worker-count knobs for page-data collection vs static generation (or share/cache the collected page-data module graph across workers).

Previously filed as #95744 (closed for missing repro link — this issue adds the public reproduction).

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: arm64
  Version: #1 SMP Mon Feb 24 16:35:16 UTC 2025
  Available memory (MB): 7838 (container capped at 4096)
  Available CPU cores: 12 (container capped at 4)
Binaries:
  Node: 22.23.1
  npm: 10.9.8
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.0-preview.5 // Latest available version is detected (16.3.0-preview.5).
  react: 19.2.0
  react-dom: 19.2.0
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Performance, Turbopack, Webpack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

Also reproduced on Vercel build machines: a production app that builds with webpack in a 16GB container OOMs under Turbopack on the 30-vCPU/60GB Turbo machine, dying 27 seconds into `Collecting page data using 14 workers`. Happy to provide `NEXT_TURBOPACK_TRACING` traces privately.

open.title: App Router: root route's server-side usePathname() is "/index" on Vercel, causing hydration mismatch (#418)
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/cyrilpsaju/nextjs-root-pathname-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction above. It is a minimal App Router app: a root layout, a route group, and a client component in the **group layout** that renders only on the root route:

```jsx
// app/(group)/chrome.js
"use client"
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation"

export function Chrome() {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  if (pathname !== "/") return null
  return <header id="chrome">root-only chrome</header>
}
```

2. Local control — behaves correctly:

```bash
npm install && npm run build && npm start
curl -s localhost:3000/    | grep -c 'id="chrome"'                 # 1
curl -s localhost:3000/    | grep -o '\\"c\\":\[[^]]*\]' | head -1  # "c":["",""]
curl -s localhost:3000/faq | grep -c 'id="chrome"'                 # 0
```

3. Deploy the same commit to Vercel, then:

```bash
curl -s https://<deployment-host>/ | grep -c 'id="chrome"'                 # 0  <-- expected 1
curl -s https://<deployment-host>/ | grep -o '\\"c\\":\[[^]]*\]' | head -1  # "c":["","index"]  <-- expected ["",""]
curl -s https://<deployment-host>/faq | grep -o '\\"c\\":\[[^]]*\]' | head -1  # "c":["","faq"]   correct
```

4. Load the deployed root route in a browser: React logs hydration error **#418**, once per load.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current (deployed to Vercel):** for the **root route only**, the server-side canonical pathname is `/index`. `usePathname()` therefore returns `/index` during SSR and `/` on the client, so a client component branching on `pathname === "/"` renders a different tree on each side. React reports hydration error #418, discards the server HTML for that subtree and re-renders it on the client. The subtree is **absent from the server-rendered HTML**.

**Expected:** `usePathname()` returns `/` on the server for the root route, matching the client — and matching the `x-matched-path: /` the response already reports.

**Evidence — the RSC Flight payload.** The Flight payload embedded in the SSR HTML carries the router's canonical path segments as `"c"`:

| route | deployed to Vercel | local `next build && next start` |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `"c":["","index"]` ❌ | `"c":["",""]` ✅ |
| `/faq` | `"c":["","faq"]` ✅ | `"c":["","faq"]` ✅ |

Additional observations:

- The response reports `x-matched-path: /`, so routing matched the root route. Only the canonical serialised into the Flight payload is `index` — which is the prerender's filename, `.next/server/app/index.html`.
- The client component's reference **is** present in the deployed Flight payload, so the server was asked to render it and it returned `null`. It is not dropped downstream by streaming or caching.
- `next build` locally produces `.next/server/app/index.html` that **does** contain the component's output.
- `next start` serves **both** `/` and `/index` with `"c":["",""]` and renders the component, so Next's own server normalises the root route.
- Deterministic: exactly one #418 per load, on fast and throttled networks, and across `x-vercel-cache: HIT` and `STALE` alike.

**Impact.** Beyond the console error, the affected subtree is missing from the SSR HTML. In a real application this meant a site header and all of its internal navigation links were absent from the server-rendered output — invisible to crawlers that do not execute JavaScript (confirmed with a Googlebot user agent) — and a bottom navigation bar server-rendered with no active tab. Measured: no layout shift (CLS 0.000), no visible flicker; the cost is the lost SSR output and the re-render.

**Temporary mitigation (not a proposed fix).** Accepting both spellings restores matching output:

```js
const isRoot = pathname === "/" || pathname === "/index"
```

Safe only because `/index` is not a routable page (it normalises to the root route). It is a compatibility shim — the underlying canonical is still wrong. Noted in case others hit this first.

### Provide environment information

```
Operating System:
  Platform: win32
  Arch: x64
  Version: Windows 11
Binaries:
  Node: 24.14.1
  npm: 11.11.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.9
  react: 19.2.4
  react-dom: 19.2.4
```

Deployed on Vercel. Reproduced on two independent Vercel projects built from the same commit, in an application with the structure above.

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Navigation, Runtime, Vercel

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

I verified the linked reproduction locally: it renders the component and reports `"c":["",""]`, as expected. I was unable to publish a **public** Vercel deployment of it — Deployment Protection is enforced on my account, so the deployment URL answers `302` to the Vercel SSO endpoint. Deploying the repo should surface the divergence; the `curl` checks in **To Reproduce** are the ones to run.

The deployed-vs-local divergence itself was observed on two Vercel production deployments of an application with this exact structure.

open.title: Streamed Suspense boundaries never reveal in documents that load hidden (background tab, occluded window, iOS standalone PWA) — vendored react-dom gates the first $RB reveal batch on requestAnimationFrame
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/jocchiuti/next-suspense-hidden-document-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install && npm run build && npm start` (the page is `force-dynamic` with a `loading.js` fallback and an async page that resolves after 1.5s, so the shell always streams before the content segment).
2. Open `http://localhost:3000` **as a document load in a hidden tab** — cmd/ctrl-click a link to it, or start the load and switch tabs before it begins — and keep the document hidden past the content delay. (Fully occluded windows on macOS/Windows and Edge sleeping tabs behave the same.)
3. Without focusing the tab, attach DevTools (`chrome://inspect`) and check:

```js
document.visibilityState        // "hidden"
document.readyState             // "complete"  — the stream fully arrived
window.$RB.length               // 2           — the reveal pair is parked
typeof window.$RT               // "undefined" — $RV never ran
document.getElementById("S:0")  // <div hidden id="S:0"> — content is in the DOM
document.getElementById("fallback") // the loading.js fallback is still live
```

4. The page stays in this state **indefinitely** while hidden — no errors anywhere. Running the page's own `window.$RV(window.$RB)` reveals the content instantly, which isolates the starved scheduling as the only blocker. Focusing the tab also un-wedges it (the parked rAF finally fires), which is why this is under-reported.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current.** The react-dom canary vendored by Next batches streamed Suspense reveals. The `$RC("B:n","S:n")` script that Next streams only pushes the `[template, content]` pair into a global `$RB` array; the actual DOM swap runs later in `$RV`. This is the `$RC` in the HTML Next 16.2.6 serves (identical in `16.3.0-canary.79`):

```js
$RC=function(a,b){if(b=document.getElementById(b))(a=document.getElementById(a))?
(a.previousSibling.data="$~",$RB.push(a,b),
2===$RB.length&&("number"!==typeof $RT
  ?requestAnimationFrame($RV.bind(null,$RB))                                    // ← only path before first paint
  :(a=performance.now(),setTimeout($RV.bind(null,$RB),2300>a&&2E3<a?2300-a:$RT+300-a))))
:b.parentNode.removeChild(b)};
```

Three things compound:

1. `$RT` is only ever set *inside* `$RV` itself (`$RV=function(a){$RT=performance.now();…}`), so on a document that has never painted, the first batch is scheduled **exclusively** via `requestAnimationFrame` — which browsers do not fire in hidden/occluded documents.
2. Every subsequent `$RC` call only pushes into `$RB` (the `2 === $RB.length` gate means nothing is ever re-scheduled), so **all** boundaries on the page pile up behind that one starved animation frame.
3. The `$~` marker opts the boundary out of client-side recovery at end of document load, so hydration doesn't rescue it either. Nothing throws.

Any document that is hidden from birth is affected: background-tab opens, occluded windows — and, worst in practice, **iOS standalone PWAs, which cold-boot with the document hidden under the splash screen**. We hit this as a launch blocker in a production App Router PWA: cold loads rendered a permanently blank page slot with the complete streamed HTML sitting in hidden `S:n` segments, and on iOS we observed launches where the parked reveal never fired even after the app became visible (unlike desktop tabs, where focusing reliably runs the parked rAF). SPA/RSC navigations never execute these inline reveal scripts, which masks the bug during development.

There is also a revealed-but-never-hydrated variant (document visible for first paint, hidden afterwards): `$RV` gates hydration retries on rAF too (`g._reactRetry&&requestAnimationFrame(g._reactRetry)`), producing a complete-looking page with dead interactivity — see scenario B in the upstream issue.

**Expected.** Suspense boundaries whose content has fully streamed should reveal (and hydrate) even if the document is hidden — e.g. fall back to `setTimeout` when the animation frame doesn't fire within a deadline (the code already has a `$RT + 300ms` setTimeout throttle branch that works fine in hidden documents), or initialise `$RT` synchronously for hidden documents, which is what the upstream fix PR does.

### Provide environment information

```

  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.4.0
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 24.15.0
  npm: 11.12.1
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 11.10.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.2.6 (also reproduced with 16.3.0-canary.79)
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.6
  react-dom: 19.2.6
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Performance, Runtime. Concretely: App Router streaming SSR — the Suspense reveal instruction set emitted by the react-dom canary vendored in `next/dist/compiled/react-dom`.

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local), Deployed (we reproduced on Vercel and on plain `next start`; production builds — `next dev` emits the same instruction set).

### Additional context

**Root cause is upstream react-dom (Fizz instruction set), already tracked with an open fix:**

- Upstream bug: [react/react#36741](https://github.com/react/react/issues/36741) (open) — same mechanism, both scenarios.
- Fix PR: [react/react#36751](https://github.com/react/react/pull/36751) (open) — initialises `$RT` synchronously when the document is hidden and via a one-shot `visibilitychange` listener, routing everything through the existing `setTimeout` branch.
- Introduced by [react/react#34230](https://github.com/react/react/pull/34230) ("[Fizz] If we haven't painted yet, wait to reveal everything until next paint", Aug 2025).

Filing here as well because Next vendors the affected canaries, so Next users can't get the fix by bumping `react-dom` — it has to ship via `next/dist/compiled/react-dom`:

- `next@16.2.6` vendors `react-dom 19.3.0-canary-3f0b9e61-20260317`.
- `next@16.3.0-canary.79` vendors `react-dom 19.3.0-canary-23def8fd-20260706` — **identical `$RC` scheduling, so this reproduces on the latest canary**.
- We checked the 16.2.7–16.2.10 release diffs: no related change. Given the impact on installed PWAs (every cold boot is a hidden-document load), please consider a 16.2.x backport once the upstream fix lands.

Nearest prior reports, for cross-reference: #94170 (closed — different variant of the same silent-no-op family: `$~` postpone marker emitted for async server components so `$RC` no-ops). Downstream, getsentry/sentry-javascript#21768 / #21836 are flaky streaming E2E tests in automation-driven tabs, which are frequently hidden/occluded — plausibly this mechanism, though we haven't verified those.

**Workaround we ship in production** (inline script in the root layout; tier 1 of our version — it just runs React's own reveal when the queue is parked):

```html
<script>
(function () {
  function reveal() {
    try {
      if (typeof $RV === "function" && window.$RB && window.$RB.length) $RV(window.$RB);
    } catch (e) {}
  }
  function arm() {
    setTimeout(reveal, 3500);
    setTimeout(reveal, 8000);
    document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", function () {
      if (document.visibilityState === "visible") setTimeout(reveal, 1200);
    });
  }
  document.readyState === "loading"
    ? document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", arm)
    : arm();
})();
</script>
```

(Our production version adds a second tier that manually swaps any boundary still `$?`/`$~` whose `S:n` segment exists — same semantics as the non-view-transition `$RV`, including firing `_reactRetry` — but the snippet above covers the common case.)

open.title: Flight payload repeats the full chunk URL list for every client module reference (~29% of SSR HTML is duplicated chunk URLs)
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/Adophlidu/next-flight-chunklist-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run build` (default Turbopack production build)
3. `npm run start`
4. `node analyze.mjs http://localhost:3000/` — the script curls the SSR HTML, decodes the `self.__next_f` flight payload, and counts chunk-URL strings in the client module reference rows.

The page is an ordinary shape: 30 small statically imported `'use client'` components plus 3 `next/dynamic` client components.

Output on `16.3.0-canary.79` (identical on latest stable `16.2.10`):

```
HTML bytes (raw)               15,869
flight payload bytes (decoded) 10,302 (64.9% of HTML)
client module reference rows   41
chunk-URL strings in flight    117
unique chunk files             5
duplication factor             23.4x
bytes of chunk-URL text        4,568 (28.8% of HTML)
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** Every client-module reference row in the flight payload —

```
N:I[moduleId, ["/_next/static/chunks/a.js", "/_next/static/chunks/b.js", ...], exportName]
```

— serializes the **entire chunk URL list of its chunk group**. Because Turbopack merges a page's client modules into a shared chunk group, every reference row on the page carries an identical copy of the same URL list. The redundant bytes grow multiplicatively as `(number of client references) × (chunk group size)`, so on real applications this dominates the document.

Measured on a real production page, https://staging.firefly.social/profile/farcaster/3 (Next.js 16.2.x + Turbopack, deployed on Vercel; publicly accessible, `node analyze.mjs <url>` from the repro works against it):

```
HTML bytes (raw)               473,786
flight payload bytes (decoded) 357,251 (75.4% of HTML)
client module reference rows   74
chunk-URL strings in flight    2,770
unique chunk files             64
duplication factor             43.3x
bytes of chunk-URL text        135,749 (28.7% of HTML)
```

74 reference rows each repeat a ~38-URL chunk list: 2,770 chunk-URL strings of which only 64 are unique, ≈136 KB of pure URL text — about 29% of the whole document (the same ~29% ratio the minimal repro shows). Before this app switched to hash-only immutable asset paths, every URL additionally carried a `?dpl=` skew-protection suffix, which pushed URL text past 200 KB per page.

Gzip absorbs most of the wire cost, but the raw bytes still have to be streamed, parsed, and held in memory on every SSR request, and they inflate TTFB-to-last-byte for the streamed document.

**Expected:** Chunk lists are deduplicated in the flight payload — e.g. each distinct chunk list is emitted once and referenced by id from the `I[...]` rows (a dictionary encoding, analogous to how the flight protocol already deduplicates repeated rows by row id). That would collapse ~136 KB of URL text to roughly the size of one chunk list.

### Provide environment information

```bash

  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 23.3.0: Wed Dec 20 21:30:59 PST 2023; root:xnu-10002.81.5~7/RELEASE_ARM64_T6030
  Available memory (MB): 36864
  Available CPU cores: 11
Binaries:

Relevant Packages:

Next.js Config:

```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Performance, Turbopack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

- Affects App Router production builds with Turbopack (Turbopack's chunk-group merging makes the per-reference list large and identical across references; webpack builds emit the same encoding but with smaller per-module chunk lists).
- Reproduces identically on latest stable `16.2.10` and `16.3.0-canary.79`, locally and deployed on Vercel.
- This is a scalability issue rather than a functional bug: payload overhead grows as `client references × chunk-group size`, so it gets quadratically worse exactly on the pages that are already the largest.

open.title: E696 `Invariant: Expected workUnitAsyncStorage to have a store` intermittently fails `next build` static export on random pages under machine load
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/discordwell/next-e696-workunit-store-race

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run repro` — loops `next build --webpack` (default 10×) under CPU spinners (`RUNS=25` for more attempts)

This is a scheduling race, so reproduction is statistical: on an idle machine the loop stays green; it fires under genuine machine-wide CPU contention. Original environment: an 18-core darwin workstation under heavy background load (leaked containers + parallel builds) — 6+ failures in one day on a ~550-static-page production app, on a **different trivial static page each time**. 12 controlled rebuilds of the identical SHA on the same machine while idle were all green (including runs at reduced QoS under 16 CPU spinners — it takes real contention). The repo README carries full instructions and the source-level analysis.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** during `Generating static pages`, a random page intermittently fails with:

```
Error [InvariantError]: Invariant: Expected workUnitAsyncStorage to have a store. This is a bug in Next.js.
```

(`__NEXT_ERROR_CODE: E696`), and with defaults (single attempt + `prerenderEarlyExit`) the whole build fails. The failing page differs each occurrence (`/auth/error`, `/auth/help`, `/assistant/activate`, …) — all trivial fully-static pages.

**Expected:** static export succeeds regardless of machine load.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.3.0
  Available memory (MB): 49152
  Available CPU cores: 18
Binaries:
  Node: 22.22.3
  npm: 10.9.8
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.1.6
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.0.0
  react-dom: 19.0.0
  typescript: 6.0.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Runtime

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local)

### Additional context

Re-files #95543, which was auto-closed — it was created via the `gh` CLI rather than this form, so the validator could not read the reproduction-link field (the link existed in the body). Per the bot's instructions, this is a new issue with the link in the correct section.

**Why it races** (analysis against 16.1.6 dist; the same code is present in canary as of 2026-07-06, so this is not fixed by upgrading):

`server/app-render/use-flight-response.js` — `getFlightResponse` memoizes the deserialized flight response **per stream at first touch**, and reads `workUnitAsyncStorage.getStore()` from whatever async context makes that first touch, throwing E696 when absent. The store is only *functionally* needed there for the `prerender-client` (canary: also `validation-client`) `process.nextTick` deferral — the throw is a context-loss tripwire.

Two windows let that first touch execute **outside** any `workUnitAsyncStorage.run(store, …)` scope:

1. **Abort-path unwind.** `app-render.js` wraps the render *calls* in `workUnitAsyncStorage.run(...)`, but the `AbortController.abort()` calls that terminate those phases (scheduled after `waitAtLeastOneReactRenderTask()`) execute in the **enclosing scope**, which carries no work-unit store. Abort listeners dispatch synchronously in the aborting context, so React's unwind work — which can reach `useFlightStream` → `getFlightResponse` — runs store-less.
2. **Backpressure resume.** React's streaming render pauses on backpressure and resumes from the **consumer's** `pull()`. During static export that consumer is the export worker's stream collector, outside the store scope. If a page's shell hasn't completed its first in-scope task before the consumer drives the stream, the memoized first touch lands store-less.

On an idle machine each page's shell completes inside its first in-scope render task, so the memoization always captures a live store and the bug never fires — which is why CI and Vercel builds look clean. Under CPU starvation, render tasks lag behind the abort/backpressure windows and a random page loses the race; a large static page count × export workers × per-page concurrency (8) gives every build many dice.

**Suggested fix shape:** carry the context across those seams explicitly — `AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot()`/`.bind()` around the abort handlers and stream handoffs, or pass the store as a parameter the way `collectSegmentData` already does (it receives the store explicitly precisely because ALS doesn't flow there).

**Workaround** (has absorbed every occurrence for us):

```js
// next.config.mjs
experimental: {
  staticGenerationRetryCount: 3,
}
```

**Related:** #86978 (same invariant during prerender, Turbopack, "only occurred locally, not on Vercel"), #92656 (same signature, auto-closed for a missing repro link), #90669 (same invariant via a different trigger — module duplication in pnpm monorepos).

open.title: Build fails with webpack when pageExtensions contains a single value
open.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/KinjiKawaguchi/nextjs-single-page-extension-webpack-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction repository and install (`pnpm install`).
2. Build with webpack (`pnpm build`, which runs `next build --webpack`).
3. The build fails with a resolve error for every app dir route.

```
Failed to compile.

app/page.tsx
Can't resolve private-next-app-dir/page
```

4. To verify the working case, check out the `control` branch (`git checkout control`) and repeat step 2. The only difference is that `pageExtensions` has two values instead of one. The build now succeeds.



### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior**

With a single-element `pageExtensions` value such as `['tsx']`, `next build --webpack` fails to resolve any app dir route and aborts. The trigger is the number of elements, not their content — `['tsx']` and `['page.tsx']` both fail, while any list with two or more values builds fine (`['tsx', 'ts']`, `['page.tsx', 'page.ts']`, etc.).

Turbopack builds succeed with the same single-element config, so this is specific to the webpack pipeline.

**Expected behavior**

A single-element `pageExtensions` list should build the same way a multi-element list does.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: linux
  Arch: x64
  Version: #85-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Sep 18 15:26:59 UTC 2025
  Available memory (MB): 1547759
  Available CPU cores: 32
Binaries:
  Node: 24.15.0
  npm: 11.12.1
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: 10.33.0
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.0-canary.78 // Latest available version is detected (16.3.0-canary.78).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.7
  react-dom: 19.2.7
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Webpack

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local)

### Additional context

I believe I found the cause. When webpack builds an app dir route, the entry goes through Next.js's internal `next-app-loader`, which receives its options serialized as a webpack query string. A query string cannot distinguish a single-element array from a plain string, so `pageExtensions: ['tsx']` reaches the loader as the string `'tsx'`. The loader does handle that case, but unlike the array case it forgets to add the leading dot (`packages/next/src/build/webpack/loaders/next-app-loader/index.ts`).

```ts
const extensions =
  typeof pageExtensions === 'string'
    ? [pageExtensions]
    : pageExtensions.map((extension) => `.${extension}`)
```

The extension list ends up as `['tsx']` instead of `['.tsx']`, so the loader tries to resolve `page` + `tsx` = `pagetsx` and fails. Adding the missing dot in `node_modules` makes both `['tsx']` and `['page.tsx']` build successfully, which I believe confirms the diagnosis. Happy to send a PR — the fix is one line plus a regression test.

#65040 reported the same config failing with a different symptom (`pageExtensions.map is not a function`) on an older version, and was auto-closed as stale and locked without a fix.

### To Reproduce

2. Run `npm install`
3. Run `npm run build` — build succeeds
4. Run `npm run start`
5. Visit `/` and `GET /api/hello`

Alternatively:

```bash
npm run dev
curl http://localhost:3000/api/hello
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior


**Expected:** `import.meta.glob` is officially supported by Turbopack in Next.js 16.3 and should follow Vite-compatible importer-relative path semantics.

In this repro:

- the Server Component page should resolve `./page-modules/*.js` to `["page-local-module"]`
- the Server Component page should resolve `../lib/modules/*.js` to `["example-module"]`
- the App Route should resolve `./modules/*.js` to `["local-module"]`
- the App Route should resolve `../../../lib/modules/*.js` to `["example-module"]`

`/api/hello` should return:

```json
{
  "localValues": ["local-module"],
  "parentValues": ["example-module"]
}
```

The page should render:

- `page-local-values`: `["page-local-module"]`
- `page-parent-values`: `["example-module"]`

**Actual on Next.js 16.3 canary (`16.3.0-canary.78`):**

}

- the page renders:

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/KinjiKawaguchi/nextjs-font-preload-multi-dot-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction repository and install (`pnpm install`).
2. Build and start (`pnpm build && pnpm start`).
3. `curl -s http://localhost:3000/ | grep 'rel="preload".*font'`
4. Nothing prints — no `<link rel="preload" as="font">` tag is present in the HTML.
5. To verify the working case, check out the `control` branch (`git checkout control`) and repeat steps 2 and 3. The `control` branch removes the `pageExtensions` config and renames the files back to `layout.tsx` / `page.tsx`. Font preload tags now appear in the HTML.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current behavior**

With `pageExtensions: ['page.tsx']`, `<link rel="preload" as="font">` tags are not emitted for fonts imported via `next/font` on any statically prerendered route. CSS and JS preload tags for the same route are still emitted correctly, so the omission is specific to fonts. The browser only discovers the font URLs after parsing CSS `@font-face` rules, which delays LCP for any text using the font.

**Expected behavior**

Font preload tags should be emitted regardless of the `pageExtensions` value. `pageExtensions` is a single top-level `next.config.js` option that applies to both the `app` and `pages` directories, and the [pageExtensions docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions) list this exact multi-dot pattern as supported:

> Then, rename your pages to have a file extension that includes `.page` (e.g. rename `MyPage.tsx` to `MyPage.page.tsx`).
> ```js
> module.exports = {
>   pageExtensions: ['page.tsx', 'page.ts', 'page.jsx', 'page.js'],
> }
> ```

**The issue does not reproduce when**

- `pageExtensions` is left at its default (font preload tags are emitted normally).
- `pageExtensions` is set to a single-extension value like `['tsx']`.
- The same file uses a single-dot extension (`layout.tsx` → font preload OK; `layout.page.tsx` → font preload missing).

CSS and JS preload continue to work in every case. The omission is specific to `next/font`.

next build (local), next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

Digging into the source, the two internal manifests emit keys in different formats for the same source file. `entryCSSFiles` / `entryJSFiles` (from `flight-manifest-plugin`) produce keys like `[project]/app/layout.page`, where only the final `.tsx` has been stripped from `layout.page.tsx`. `next-font-manifest.app` (from `next-font-manifest-plugin`) produces keys like `[project]/app/page`, where all extensions have been stripped so `.page` is gone.

At runtime both the CSS/JS preload and font preload paths normalize the source path with the same regex.

```ts
filePath.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, '')
```

That strips exactly one extension (`.tsx`), producing `layout.page` / `page.page`. CSS/JS lookups succeed because the manifest key `layout.page` matches. Font lookups fail because the manifest key `page` does not match `page.page`, so `getPreloadableFonts` returns null and no preload tag is emitted.

The relevant files (paths from `packages/next/src`) are `server/app-render/get-preloadable-fonts.tsx` (font lookup regex), `server/app-render/get-css-inlined-link-tags.tsx` (CSS/JS lookup with the same regex), `build/webpack/plugins/next-font-manifest-plugin.ts` (font manifest key), and `build/webpack/plugins/flight-manifest-plugin.ts` (CSS/JS manifest key).

Aligning the font manifest key format with the CSS/JS manifest key format (i.e. retain the pre-`.tsx` stem) looks like the smallest diff. I have not verified this in a PR yet; happy to send one if maintainers agree with the direction.

**Related issues**

I searched existing issues for `getPreloadableFonts`, `pageExtensions font preload`, `next-font-manifest`, and `multi-dot pageExtensions`, and did not find a direct duplicate.

#62332 ("Font preload not working as expected") has the same symptom of font preload tags missing, but none of the sub-reports there involve `pageExtensions`. Reported conditions include Windows-specific behavior, a `VERCEL_CLI_VERSION` regression around 33.5.1, a `next dev --turbo` regression in 15.4.4, and `next/font/local` on default `pageExtensions`. The reproduction in this issue is independent of all of those. It happens on Linux, on `next start` without the Vercel CLI, without Turbopack in dev, using `next/font/google`, and cleanly toggles on and off with the `pageExtensions` value. If maintainers consider this a facet of #62332 rather than a distinct bug, feel free to close and I will move the analysis there as a comment.

#53473 / #91746 report the `no-html-link-for-pages` ESLint rule not respecting custom `pageExtensions`. Different feature area, but the same underlying pattern of a Next.js internal hardcoding single-dot extension assumptions. Flagging in case there is a shared fix opportunity.

  cacheComponents: true,
  htmlLimitedBots: /GoogleOther|MySpecialBot|Twitterbot/i,
};
